plan_a_advantages: Incorporates interval training for speed development.
More balanced approach with aerobic base building and speed work.
Includes strength training to improve power and stability.
More varied session types (intervals, aerobic, strength).
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on threshold training, which can be beneficial for sustained effort.
Long runs are consistently at an easy pace, promoting endurance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates interval training and a more varied approach to long runs. While both plans include long runs, Plan A’s inclusion of interval sessions directly targets speed development, a crucial component for improving race times. Furthermore, Plan A’s structure feels more balanced, with a greater emphasis on building a solid aerobic base alongside specific speed work, whereas Plan B leans heavily into extended, easy-paced runs which, while beneficial for endurance, may not be the most efficient way to boost speed. The inclusion of strength training in Plan A also addresses a key area often neglected in trail running training.
